investigations.question: Can a user of the omnipaxos_runtime actor layer reach the core's documented log compaction (OmniPaxos::trim / OmniPaxos::snapshot) at all - does any handle method, any Command variant or any internal call the actor makes into the core provide that path?
investigations.hypothesis: No path exists: spawn_actor consumes the OmniPaxos instance by value, the handle keeps only channels and a capacity (no accessor for the instance and no trim/snapshot method), the actor's Command enum has no compaction variant, and nothing in the actor calls op.trim()/op.snapshot(), so a runtime-only user cannot bound the log's growth.
investigations.discriminator: Source inspection of all three places a path could exist: every public method on OmniPaxosHandle, every Command variant in the actor protocol, and every call the actor makes into the core. Finding a compaction command, a handle method or any internal call reaching trim/snapshot would refute the hypothesis; documentation stating that compaction is deliberately out of scope would limit it to a capability gap rather than an omission.

interpretations.rationale: Source-only current account; no execution. The core documents compaction as a user operation on the instance: OmniPaxos::trim(trim_index: Option<usize>) -> Result<(), CompactionErr> deletes entries up to an index or up to the minimum index accepted by all servers, and OmniPaxos::snapshot(compact_idx, local_only) trims and snapshots up to the decided index (omni_paxos.rs:242-262). The runtime layer takes that instance away from the caller - spawn_actor::<T, B, R>(op: OmniPaxos<T, B>, cfg) consumes it by value (handle.rs:295) - and the handle it returns carries only cmd_tx, events_rx, outgoing_rx, incoming_tx and decided_channel_capacity, with no accessor back to the instance. The actor's client protocol has no compaction request: Command lists Append, AppendNotify, CurrentLeader, DecidedIdx, ReadDecidedSuffix, SubscribeDecided, Reconfigure, TryBecomeLeader and Reconnected, and nothing else (event.rs:90-128), and the actor itself never calls op.trim()/op.snapshot() - the only 'trim' in the layer is trim_oldest over its own outgoing buffer (actor.rs:239, 715-720). The layer presents itself as the way to run the core without driving it: its crate docs say the runtime removes the need to fetch and send messages manually and that the actor owns that work (lib.rs:7-15), and the shipped example uses only the handle. So a runtime-only user has no reachable path to the core's documented compaction contract, and the log can only grow: the finding is an omitted operation of the layer that owns the instance, with an operational consequence (unbounded storage) rather than a safety or liveness one. Counter-limitations kept in force: (a) the layer nowhere claims feature parity with the core, so the claim rests on the absence of any path (three places inspected) plus the layer's own framing as the complete way to use the core; (b) the consequence is bounded by what the storage backend does on its own (e.g. a backend could refuse writes when full, which would turn an operational issue into a write error for the actor - not measured); (c) the same layer does expose other core-facing operations through the handle (append, append_notify, reconfigure, read_decided_suffix, current_leader, decided_idx, try_become_leader, reconnected, subscribe_decided), so this is a specific omission rather than a general policy of exposing nothing beyond writes.
limitations: Source-only account: the absence of a path is established by inspecting the handle's methods, the Command enum and the actor's calls into the core, not by an execution.
The consequence (unbounded log growth) is not measured, and the storage backend's behaviour when it fills is not examined.
Whether the omission is a deliberate scope decision is not documented anywhere in the snapshot; the account therefore treats it as an omitted operation rather than as a policy.
